title: Augmented two-term resolution of finite coefficients over completed coefficients
statement: Fix universes d,t,u, a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, a scheme Y in universe t, a finite-field datum D in universe d with characteristic unequal to l, and n a natural number. Put R equal to the completed integral coefficient ring sheaf on the pro-etale site of Y. The restriction to R of the finite coefficient unit at level n, placed in degree zero, admits an augmented resolution Q. The complex Q is K-flat, is zero outside degrees -1 and 0, and its terms in these degrees are isomorphic to the R-module unit. The augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. The restriction functor and coefficient objects are exactly those of [def-sf-integral-hom-reduction-models] and [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction].

proof.text: Use the DVR of integers of E and its standard quotient resolution: multiplication by a uniformizer power between two free rank-one modules, with augmentation to the quotient.

Apply the constant-sheaf construction and extend to the completed sheaf. Flatness and the completed reduction identification preserve the augmented resolution and identify its target with the actual restricted finite unit. The terms remain unit modules and a bounded flat complex is K-flat.

theorem integralReduction_twoTerm_resolution (n : ℕ) :
    let R := completedIntegralCommRingSheaf l E Y D hl
    ∃ (Q : CochainComplex (Modules.{t, u} Y R) ℤ)
      (_ : flat.{t, u} Y R Q)
      (_ : ∀ k : ℤ, k ≠ -1 → k ≠ 0 → IsZero (Q.X k))
      (_ : Q.X (-1) ≅ (show Modules.{t, u} Y R from SheafOfModules.unit
        ((sheafCompose (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology Y)
          (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u (t + 1)} RingCat.{max u (t + 1)})).obj R)))
      (_ : Q.X 0 ≅ (show Modules.{t, u} Y R from SheafOfModules.unit
        ((sheafCompose (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology Y)
          (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u (t + 1)} RingCat.{max u (t + 1)})).obj R)))
      (epsilon : Q ⟶
        ((scalarReductionRestriction l E Y n).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
          ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (scalarReductionTarget l E Y n) 0).obj
            (SheafOfModules.unit (integralCoefficientSheaf l E Y n)))),
      QuasiIso epsilon
